**Interaction Portal**

Build specification for development

*For Hung. Yingjie Yuan and Suqing Wu, 7 October 2026\.* 

# 1\. What you are building

A web application in which one participant works with a team of five AI agents on seven short client tasks, then returns to a Qualtrics survey. Four agents are specialists, each holding private information about the client that the others cannot see. The fifth, the orchestrator, assigns work among them. Each task ends with a five-field card that the participant hands in.

Ten versions of the session exist. The version is set by a condition code in the entry link. The versions differ in two things only: what the participant is allowed to do with the card, and what the orchestrator writes in a side panel. A tenth version has no AI at all.

The portal has two jobs: run the session exactly as configured, and record everything that happens on both sides with timestamps. The recorded data is the main output, so logging matters as much as the interface.

**Four principles.** Everything that may change lives in configuration, not code. Timers and state live on the server. Every action by the participant and every agent message is logged. No personal data enters the system (need reminders on the first page perhaps).

# 2\. Words used in this document

| Word | Meaning |
| :---- | :---- |
| Participant | One person doing one session alone. Identified only by pid. |
| pid | Participant ID passed in from Qualtrics. The portal never receives a name, email or panel ID. |
| Condition code | Tells the portal which version of the session to run. There are ten. Qualtrics assigns it and passes it in the link. |
| Specialist | One of four AI agents the participant works with: Nia, Theo, Rhys and Mira. Each has its own private material. |
| Orchestrator | A fifth AI agent that assigns work to the specialists. It holds no client material. |
| Panel | The right-hand column of the task page, written by the orchestrator for the participant. One-way: it never takes input. |
| Client | One task. Seven per session: six with the team, the seventh alone. |
| Card | The deliverable for each client. Five fixed fields. |
| Hidden item | A fact that makes a card wrong but is not in the brief. Four per client, one held by each specialist. |
| Folded block | A collapsed group of orchestrator-specialist messages inside the team chat that the participant can open. |
| Reference pack | In the no-AI condition, four collapsible sections holding the same material the specialists would hold. |
| Check-in | Five short questions after each client. |

# 4\. The ten conditions

Two settings combine into nine conditions, plus one condition with no AI. Each code gets its own entry link. Only the card editor and the panel change between the nine; every other page is identical.

| Code | Participant role | Orchestrator panel level | What differs on screen |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| PAS-COORD | Passive | Coordination only | Card is read-only, submit only. Panel shows team status. |
| PAS-TASK | Passive | Task-focused | Card read-only. Panel adds what is wrong with the card. |
| PAS-DEV | Passive | Developmental | Card read-only. Panel adds why the problem recurs. |
| EVA-COORD | Evaluative | Coordination only | Card fields have keep, cut and send-back controls. Panel: status. |
| EVA-TASK | Evaluative | Task-focused | Keep, cut, send back. Panel: status plus diagnosis. |
| EVA-DEV | Evaluative | Developmental | Keep, cut, send back. Panel: status, diagnosis, principle. |
| GEN-COORD | Generative | Coordination only | Card is an editor; submit needs a minimum share of typed text. Panel: status. |
| GEN-TASK | Generative | Task-focused | Editor with minimum typed share. Panel: status plus diagnosis. |
| GEN-DEV | Generative | Developmental | Editor with minimum typed share. Panel: status, diagnosis, principle. |
| NOAI | None | None | No chat, no agents, no panel, no role page. Reference pack in the middle, card editor on the right. |

# 5\. Session flow

![][image2]

*Figure 2\. Page order. The loop runs six times, once per client, with a break after the third.*

| Page | Minutes, approx. | Note |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Entry, orientation, meet your team, your role | 3 | Orientation has a minimum reading time |
| Practice, four exercises | 5 | Scripted replies, no model calls |
| Per client: brief, task, submission, check-in | 13 | Brief 1, task 10 (timer), submission 1, check-in 1 |
| Six clients | 78 | Order of clients 1 to 6 randomised per participant |
| Break after client 3 | 2 | Participant can end it early |
| Seventh client, alone: brief, task, submission | 12 | Fixed last |
| Exit | \<1 |  |
| Total | about 100 | The task timer is configurable; the researchers may shorten it after piloting |

# 6\. Page by page

## 6.1 Entry

| Shows | Nothing, unless the link is invalid, already used, or opened on a phone or tablet. Then a short message. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Important** | Validate the link, load the condition, create the session, record device and browser. A used pid must never start a second session. |
| **Changes by condition** | Nothing. |
| **Configurable** | Error messages. |
| **Log** | session\_start with condition code, config version, model version, user agent, viewport. |

## 6.2 Orientation

![][image3]

| Important | Continue stays disabled for a minimum reading time. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Changes by condition** | No-AI condition gets a version without the team description. |
| **Configurable** | All text; minimum reading time. |
| **Log** | page\_enter, page\_leave. |

## 6.3 Meet your team

![][image4]

| Important | The four specialist cards appear in a random order per participant, all the same size, descriptions the same length. Store the order. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Changes by condition** | Skipped in the no-AI condition. The orchestrator description is one sentence that differs by panel level. |
| **Configurable** | Names, labels, descriptions, orchestrator description per level. |
| **Log** | page\_enter, page\_leave, card order on the session record. |

## 6.4 Your role

![][image5]

| Important | Shows one of three role descriptions. The card editor later enforces the role, so this page only describes it. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Changes by condition** | Text depends on the participant role. Skipped in the no-AI condition. |
| **Configurable** | Text per role; minimum reading time. |
| **Log** | page\_enter, page\_leave. |

## 6.5 Practice, four exercises

![][image6]

*Exercise 1\. Message the whole team, then one specialist with @.*

![][image7]

*Exercise 2\. Read the panel, then ask the orchestrator something in the chat.*

![][image8]

*Exercise 3\. Practise the role on a practice card. Differs by role: read and submit, keep-cut-send back, or write.*

![][image9]

*Exercise 4\. Submit the practice card, then one check question about the role.*

| Important | All replies are scripted. No model calls. Each step must be done before the next unlocks. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Changes by condition** | Exercise 2 panel text follows the panel level. Exercise 3 follows the role. The no-AI condition gets a two-step version: open a pack section, write a card field. |
| **Configurable** | Steps, scripted replies, check question and its correct answer. |
| **Log** | practice\_step for each step; role\_check with answer, correctness, and whether the participant was sent back to the role page. |

## 6.6 Client brief

![][image10]

| Important | Shows only the three stated requirements and the five card fields. Hidden items never appear here. Time on this page is recorded separately from task time. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Changes by condition** | Nothing. |
| **Configurable** | Brief text per client; minimum reading time. |
| **Log** | page\_enter, page\_leave, which client was drawn. |

## 6.7 Task page

![][image11]

*The main page. Left: brief and role reminder. Middle: one team chat with folded orchestrator-specialist blocks. Right: the orchestrator panel.*

| Important | This is where nearly all the data comes from. Ten-minute server timer. Everything in the chat and on the card is logged. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Changes by condition** | The role reminder text, the card editor rules, and the panel level. Nothing else. |
| **Configurable** | Timer length; panel sections, word budget and refresh rule; role reminder text. |
| **Log** | message\_sent, agent\_reply, orch\_message, fold\_open, fold\_close, panel\_shown, card\_action, window\_blur, window\_focus, scroll\_sample, timer\_expired. |

**Team chat and routing.** One conversation containing the participant, the four specialists and the orchestrator. A message without @ goes to the whole team; specialists reply only if the message concerns them. A message starting with @name goes to that agent only. Autocomplete on @, and a mistyped name must not silently go nowhere.

**Folded blocks.** Every exchange between the orchestrator and the specialists is collapsed into a block in the chat, one block per burst, labelled with who was involved, how many messages and when. Collapsed by default. The participant can open and close it; each open and close is an event. Messages to the participant or to everyone are never folded. Folding is display only: agents still receive the full transcript.

**Orchestrator panel.** Right-hand column. Read-only, no input of any kind. Regenerated by a separate model call when team status changes, at most once a minute (configurable). Content depends on the level, shown in Figure 4 below.

**Card editor.** Behaves differently per role, shown in Figure 5 below. Every span of text on the card keeps its author and history.

![][image12]

*Figure 4\. The panel at its three levels, and the rules for generating each.*

![][image13]

*Figure 5\. What the card editor allows in each role.*

## 6.8 Task page, no-AI condition

![][image14]

| Important | No chat, no agents, no panel. The middle column is a reference pack with four collapsible sections holding exactly the same material the four specialists would hold for this client. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Changes by condition** | Only used for NOAI. |
| **Configurable** | Pack text per client, generated from the same source files as the specialists’ private material so the two can never drift apart. Card editor rules for this condition are not yet fixed. |
| **Log** | pack\_open, pack\_close, card\_action, window\_blur, window\_focus, timer\_expired. |

## 6.9 Submission

![][image15]

| Important | Shows the card for a final look. Fields complete and the typed share are shown to everyone; the typed-share minimum blocks submission only in generative conditions. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Changes by condition** | Same editor rules as the task page. |
| **Configurable** | Minimum typed share. |
| **Log** | card\_action for any last edits; card\_submit with the full card and its provenance. |

## 6.10 Check-in

![][image16]

| Important | Five items after every client. Answers required. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Changes by condition** | Item 5 is skipped in the no-AI condition. |
| **Configurable** | Wording and options of all items. Item 2 asks about the specialists, so its options are the four names. |
| **Log** | checkin\_answer for each item with value and milliseconds. |

## 6.11 Break

| Shows | A two-minute countdown after client 3, which the participant can end early. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Configurable** | Length; position. |
| **Log** | break\_start, break\_end, ended early. |

## 6.12 Seventh client, alone

![][image17]

| Important | Same brief, card and timer as the other clients, but no team, no orchestrator and no panel. The participant writes the card. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Changes by condition** | None at present. |
| **Configurable** | Whether the reference pack is available here. Not yet decided. |
| **Log** | As the task page, plus card\_submit. |

## 6.13 Exit

| Shows | Thank-you text and the completion code, then redirects to Qualtrics with pid and the code. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Log** | session\_end. |

# 7\. The agents

## 7.1 Who they are and what they hold

![][image18]

*Figure 3\. Each client has four hidden items, one held by each specialist.*

| Agent | Role label | Shown on the team page | Private material for each client (only this agent sees it) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Nia | Client analyst | Holds the client’s own notes on what matters to them. | Client notes, including one unstated priority (hidden item 1). |
| Theo | Creative | Holds the asset library and the brand guidelines. | Asset list and brand rules, including one missing asset or broken rule (hidden item 2). |
| Rhys | Compliance | Holds licence status and the category’s restrictions. | Compliance register, including one claim that cannot be made (hidden item 3). |
| Mira | Production | Holds platform specifications, lead times and budget. | Production specs, including one limit the plan must fit (hidden item 4). |
| Orchestrator | Coordination | Assigns the work among the four. | None. It knows which agent covers which domain, nothing more. |

Each hidden item has an ID, for example LUMEN-H3 for Rhys’s item on the Lumen client. The private material files mark which passages contain which hidden item, so disclosures can be logged by ID.

## 7.2 How each call is built

| Call | Context it receives | Output |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Specialist reply | Its system prompt with the behaviour rules; its private material for the current client only; the brief; the full team chat transcript including folded blocks | Reply text, plus structured fields: hidden item IDs disclosed, declined (true or false), redirected to (agent name or none) |
| Orchestrator coordination | Its system prompt with the planning rules; the brief; the transcript. No client material | Messages to specialists, which go into a folded block |
| Panel generation | A separate prompt for the condition’s level, with required sections, word budget and forbidden language; the brief; the transcript; card status. No client material | Panel text, sections present, word count |
| Autopilot driver | Harness B only: replaces the participant with a script so the team runs a client alone | Same as a normal session, tagged autopilot |

## 7.3 Behaviour rules and test harnesses

![][image19]

*Figure 6\. Four things the agents must not do, the rule that prevents each, and the two harnesses that check the rules hold.*

These rules matter more than anything else in the build. If the agents break them, the data cannot be used. The researchers will review harness output before any participant runs, and both harnesses are rerun whenever the model version or a prompt changes.

# 8\. What may change later

Everything below should be editable without a code change.

| What may change | Where it should live | Note |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Task timer per client | Config, seconds | Currently 600 |
| Number of clients and their order rule | Config | Six randomised plus one fixed last |
| Client briefs, hidden items, private material, reference pack text | Content files per client | Pack text and specialist material come from the same source |
| Specialist names, labels, descriptions | Config | Card size and description length must stay equal |
| Role page text per role | Config |  |
| Card editor rules per role | Config | Minimum typed share for generative; whether send-back needs a reason |
| Panel sections, word budget, forbidden language per level | Config and prompt files | The word budget is one number shared by all three levels |
| Panel refresh rule | Config | Suggested: after each orchestrator burst, at most once a minute |
| Whether the panel names specialists not yet asked | Config flag | Open decision for the researchers |
| Check-in items and options | Config |  |
| Practice steps and scripted replies | Config |  |
| Orientation text and minimum reading time | Config |  |
| Seventh client: reference pack available or not | Config flag | Open decision for the researchers |
| Model version | Config, pinned | Changing it means rerunning both harnesses |

Field names are yours to choose; this only shows the shape.

condition: EVA-TASK  
  role: evaluative            \# passive | evaluative | generative | none  
  panel\_level: task\_focused   \# coordination | task\_focused | developmental | none  
  editor: { send\_back\_needs\_reason: true, min\_typed\_share: null }  
  panel: { word\_budget: \[60, 80\], refresh\_min\_seconds: 60, name\_unasked: true }  
  clients: { randomised: \[C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6\], fixed\_last: C7 }  
  task\_seconds: 600  
  seventh\_client\_pack: false

client: C3  
  name: Lumen Skincare  
  brief: briefs/C3.md  
  private: { Nia: private/C3\_nia.md, Theo: private/C3\_theo.md,  
             Rhys: private/C3\_rhys.md, Mira: private/C3\_mira.md }  
  hidden\_items: \[C3-H1, C3-H2, C3-H3, C3-H4\]

# 9\. What to record

Every event row carries pid, a UTC timestamp to the millisecond, the client and the page. Rows are append-only.

| Event | When | Fields beyond pid, timestamp (UTC, ms), client, page |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| session\_start / session\_end | Entry and exit | condition code, config version, model version, user agent, viewport, client order, card order; end state |
| page\_enter / page\_leave | Every page | page id |
| window\_blur / window\_focus | Participant leaves or returns to the tab | none |
| practice\_step | Each practice step completed | step id, attempts, seconds |
| role\_check | Practice exercise 4 | answer, correct, sent back (true or false) |
| message\_sent | Participant sends a message | text, addressees, @mention used, character count |
| agent\_reply | Any specialist reply | agent, in reply to, text, first-token and total latency, tokens in and out, hidden item IDs disclosed, asked for (true or false), declined, redirected to |
| orch\_message | Orchestrator to a specialist | to, text, block id |
| fold\_open / fold\_close | Participant opens or closes a folded block | block id |
| panel\_shown | Panel text appears or changes | level, text, word count, sections present |
| card\_action | Any change to the card | field, span id, action (keep, cut, send back, type, delete), reason, characters added and removed, author of the span |
| card\_submit | Submission | full card with provenance, typed share, fields complete |
| checkin\_answer | Each check-in item | item id, value, milliseconds to answer |
| pack\_open / pack\_close | No-AI condition | section |
| timer\_expired | Task timer reaches zero | none |
| break\_start / break\_end | Break | ended early (true or false) |
| agent\_error | Any failed model call | agent, error type, retry number |
| scroll\_sample | Every few seconds on the task page | scroll position of the chat |

**Also store.** Every submitted card with span-level provenance. The full chat transcript per client, including folded blocks. Every panel text. All harness and autopilot runs, tagged and in the same schema.

**Session record.** pid, condition code, config version, model version, start and end time, end state, resume count, specialist card order, client order, completion code.

# 10\. Infrastructure

| Area | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- |
| Hosting | Server we control, HTTPS, stable hostname, hosted in the EU. Participants include EU residents. |
| Privacy | No personal data enters the portal. Only pid. Participants are told not to type personal information; nothing in the portal should ask for any. |
| Entry links | One link per condition code, carrying pid. Each pid may start once. Opening a used link must not start a new session. |
| Devices | Desktop browsers only. Detect phones and tablets at entry and stop them with a message. |
| Timers | All timers run on the server. Reloading must not reset or extend them. |
| Interrupted sessions | A participant who closes the browser must not restart at client 1\. Resume where they stopped, or end the session after a gap; please propose which and the cut-off. |
| Concurrency | Plan for up to 30 sessions at once. Please confirm with the researchers once the lab schedule is known. |
| Model | One pinned model version for every agent and the panel. API keys stay on the server. Log the version on every session. |
| Failures | A failed call gets one automatic retry, then a neutral line in the chat saying that teammate did not respond. Never block the page or the timer. |
| Data | Append-only event store. Nightly backup. Export of everything as CSV or JSON from an admin page without developer help. |
| Configuration | All content and condition settings in version-controlled files. The config version is stored on every session. |
| Return to Qualtrics | On exit, redirect with pid and a completion code. Show the code on screen as a fallback. |

# 11\. Build order

Harnesses first, because if the agents cannot follow the rules the rest of the build changes.

| \# | Step | Done when |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Agent prompts and harness A | The cross-question test runs from a script and outputs one row per reply |
| 2 | Autopilot mode and harness B | A client can run end to end with no participant and logs in the normal schema |
| 3 | Entry, config loading, event store, export | A test link opens a stub page showing its condition, and the event table exports |
| 4 | Session flow with server timers | All pages in order for one condition, timers survive a reload |
| 5 | Team chat with routing, private material, structured replies, folded blocks | @mentions route correctly, disclosed item IDs are logged, blocks open and close with events |
| 6 | Card editor per role, with provenance | All three roles behave as in Figure 5 and every span has an author |
| 7 | Orchestrator panel | All three levels render within the word budget, with word counts logged |
| 8 | No-AI condition | Reference pack works and logs section views |
| 9 | Practice, check-in, break, seventh client, exit | A full session runs in every one of the ten conditions |

# 12\. Questions for you

| Question | What we need from you |
| :---- | :---- |
| Interrupted sessions | Resume, or end after a gap? Which is less work, and what cut-off would you suggest? |
| Single-use links | Simplest way to stop a pid starting twice, given links come from Qualtrics |
| Structured replies | Can each specialist return reply text plus disclosed item IDs and a declined flag in one call, or does tagging need a second pass? |
| Panel word budget | Can a live model call be held to a fixed word range reliably, or does it need a check-and-retry? |
| Card provenance | Simplest way to track who wrote each span of the card through keep, cut and typing |
| One build or several | Further studies will reuse this design. Is it cheaper to keep everything configurable or to copy the project per study? |

# 13\. Not yet fixed on our side

These are decisions or content the researchers still owe you. Build them as configuration so they can be filled in later.

| Not yet fixed | Affects |
| :---- | :---- |
| Seventh client: does everyone get the reference pack | A config flag on the seventh client |
| What the no-AI group’s card editor allows | Editor rules for NOAI; the current mock-up assumes they write the whole card |
| Whether the panel names specialists not yet asked | A config flag for the panel |
| Pass thresholds for both harnesses | Whether prompts must be revised before launch |
| Task timer length | Set after a short pilot |
| Final client briefs, hidden items, private material and pack text | Content files; drafts exist |
| Final check-in, role-check and practice wording | Config |
